pages.text: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ gives out heat (ΔH = −92.4 kJ/mol) and halves the gas (ΔS = −198 J/mol·K). So ΔG° = ΔH − TΔS rises with temperature, and the equilibrium constant K = e^(−ΔG°/RT) falls: cold and pressed gives the most ammonia. But the iron only turns the gas over fast when it is hot (Arrhenius, Eₐ ≈ 100 kJ/mol). Hence the compromise: about 450 °C and 200 atm.

$(thing)Limits$(): The iron catalyst is sintering (above 550 °C); The vessel is over its rated pressure.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Ammonia made per pass: how much there is at equilibrium, times how fast it gets there.
